clue.text: A term seems maybe term without end

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of seems could be arranged another way
the second word term loses its final letter, its end

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a school period seems to go on endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns SEEMS into SEMES; 'without end' cuts the M off the second 'term', leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A semester is one of the halves into which an academic year is divided, a term of study.

clue.text: The way a posh frock can appear in disco lighting

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a robe is a grand, formal gown

explanation.surface: A glamorous dress shows up under the flashing lights of a dance club.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a flashing lamp, a staple of nightclub dance floors.

clue.text: To a certain degree parasites show animosity

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a particular university degree
lice are parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Parasites are said to be somewhat hostile.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is ill will, a desire to harm someone.

clue.text: A shrub a French writer raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the writer's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French novelist and philosopher

explanation.surface: A French author grew a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose berries are used as a spice.

clue.text: Accomplishment put to the best advantage

explanation.surface: A feat is made the most of.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun an exploit is a daring deed or feat; as a verb, to make full use of something.

clue.text: China has taken the cup!

parts.note: sounds like a sporting headline about a nation winning a trophy, but it is a piece of crockery holding a teacup

explanation.surface: A headline announces that China has won a sporting trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: China here is porcelain, and the cup is a teacup resting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is a small china dish on which a cup stands.

clue.text: Meant to change around some rooms

indicators.note: around signals that the rearranged letters surround another piece
to change tells us the letters of meant are rearranged

parts.note: a part of something is some of it

explanation.surface: Someone means to reorganise a few rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'to change' gives AMENT, which goes 'around' PART; 'some' reads as a quantity of rooms, but it is the PART.
explanation.definitionFit: An apartment is a flat, a set of rooms used as a home.

clue.text: Critical of the top man over unpaid debts

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: CAPT, captain, is the man in charge
IOUs are notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: Someone criticises the boss for leaving bills unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious means fault-finding, always ready to criticise.

clue.text: Plasterer wanting the right finish hesitating repeatedly

parts.note: an end is a finish

indicators.note: repeatedly means the hesitation sound comes twice

parts.note: er is the noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A plasterer who wants a perfect finish keeps dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: A renderer applies render, a coat of plaster or cement, to walls.

clue.text: A great many work in turns to produce such tasty food

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the word for turns

parts.note: rolls are turns or revolutions
M, a thousand in Roman numerals, is a great many
OP, opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Lots of effort, taken in shifts, produces a delicious meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rollmops are rolled pickled herring fillets, a savoury delicacy.

clue.text: The big fish may take no part

indicators.note: may take hints that the letters of no part could take a different form

explanation.surface: A large fish might decline to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarpon is a large silvery game fish of warm Atlantic waters.

clue.text: Form of hose covering only the foot

indicators.note: form of means the letters of hose are given a new shape

explanation.surface: A kind of stocking that covers just the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is footwear that encloses the foot but not the leg.

clue.text: Support ministers creating a scene

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the cloth is a collective term for the clergy

explanation.surface: Backing government ministers causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' looks political but means clergy, known collectively as 'the cloth'; 'a scene' sounds like a fuss, but is the painted scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted curtain at the back of a stage, showing the scenery.

clue.text: Now and again?

parts.note: reads as occasionally, but cryptically it means once now and once more again, so on two occasions

explanation.surface: A question about doing something occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something now and then again means doing it on two occasions.

clue.text: Some people, if retired early, worry

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, the run inside if retired

explanation.surface: Some people fret about what happens if they retire early.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and uneasy.

clue.text: Saved about the hundred pounds intended

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, about
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra
to have aimed is to have intended

explanation.surface: Someone saved roughly the hundred pounds they had planned to.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclaimed means recovered or rescued, as land saved from the sea.

clue.text: Put an end to running water, and sharp!

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, flowing water
cute can mean shrewd or clever, sharp

explanation.surface: An order to turn off a running tap, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To execute someone is to put them to death, ending their life.

clue.text: A girl sitting between her parents to see TV programme

indicators.note: sitting between places the girl in the middle of the parents

parts.note: pa and ma are her father and mother
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl sits between mum and dad to watch television.
explanation.definitionFit: Panorama is a long-running BBC current-affairs television series.

clue.text: Quietly venomous creature — one going on and on

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a rattler is a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: A softly spoken but poisonous creature that never stops talking.
explanation.definitionFit: A prattler is someone who chatters on endlessly about trivia.

clue.text: A crop — it could be fruit

indicators.note: could be means the letters of a crop and it could form something else

explanation.surface: A harvest that might turn out to be fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a soft orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Mark is second

explanation.surface: A remark that a sign means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a check mark, and also a moment, as in 'just a tick'.

clue.text: Portly egghead's destiny

parts.note: portly means fat
the head of the word egg is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stout intellectual meets their destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual, but here it is the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is the fortune or destiny that awaits someone.

clue.text: Music — food for devotees!

parts.note: fans are devotees; one fan here
fare is food

explanation.surface: Music is described as nourishment for enthusiasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short flourish of trumpets.

clue.text: All out industrial action

explanation.surface: Everyone walks out in an industrial dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: In tenpin bowling a strike knocks all the pins out with one ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowling strike topples every pin; a workers' strike is a stoppage of labour.

clue.text: Wise words for modern times

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the modern era of dating
ages are times or eras

explanation.surface: Sayings of wisdom suited to the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: Adages are proverbs, short sayings that express a general truth.

clue.text: Old Roman place, very large, on backward little island

parts.note: OS, outsize, means very large

indicators.note: backward means the word for little island is read in reverse

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: An ancient Roman town, sizeable, sits on a tiny island.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the port of ancient Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: Anything but modest once called outside

indicators.note: outside means the word for called goes round once

parts.note: cited means called or summoned, as to court

explanation.surface: Someone who was once summoned is far from humble.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceited means vain, having an excessively high opinion of oneself.

clue.text: No longer scoff and leave

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
to scoff is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone stops gobbling food and departs.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission for a pupil to be absent from school, a leave of absence.

clue.text: Pop back and see the doctor in confidence

indicators.note: back means the word for pop is read in reverse

parts.note: pa and pop both mean father
lo is an old word meaning see or behold
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Dad goes back to consult the doctor privately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP; 'in confidence' looks like 'privately', but confidence is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assurance and poise under pressure.

clue.text: Pointed to record dealers in collaboration

parts.note: to tape is to record
a ring is a group of dealers acting together to fix prices

explanation.surface: A suggestion to record traders working together.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapering means narrowing gradually to a point.

clue.text: Wear a false beard

indicators.note: false indicates the letters of a beard are not in their true order

explanation.surface: An instruction to put on a fake beard as a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To abrade is to wear away by rubbing.

clue.text: Ill at ease without the others?

parts.note: the rest means the others
less means minus, without

explanation.surface: Someone feels uneasy when left without company.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to settle, uneasy.
